claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
(2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.note: This establishes what an answer must contain, not the procedure for filing it.

claims.claim: File the response with the court clerk.
A general denial is allowed when the complaint in a limited civil case is unverified.
claims.quote: (d) If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.
claims.note: This supports the type of denial, not the use of a particular form.

claims.claim: PLD-050 is the short general denial form.
claims.note: PLD-050 was named but not provided.

claims.claim: PLD-050 may be used in any unverified limited civil case.
claims.note: The statute does not identify PLD-050. The citation description is not the form text and cannot establish its restrictions.

claims.claim: The limited civil amount-in-controversy ceiling is $35,000, inclusive.
claims.quote: (a) The amount in controversy does not exceed thirty-five thousand dollars ($35,000).
claims.note: The ceiling is a necessary condition.

claims.claim: A claim of $35,000 or less is a limited civil case.
claims.quote: an action or special proceeding shall be treated as a limited civil case only if all of the following conditions are satisfied:
claims.note: Amount alone does not establish classification. Subsections (b) and (c) also restrict the relief sought, and subsection (a) excludes attorneys’ fees, interest, and costs from the amount in controversy.

claims.claim: A person who cannot afford the filing fee can ask for a fee waiver.
claims.note: No fee-waiver eligibility or procedure text was provided.

claims.claim: Use form FW-001 to request the fee waiver.
claims.note: FW-001 was named but not provided.

flags.text: “Any” extends the statutory permission for a general denial to a form whose instructions were not supplied. The citation mentions assigned claims over $1,000, but the scope of that restriction cannot be checked.
Relying on the blanket PLD-050 instruction could result in a defective response and risk default if the form is unavailable for the claim.
The draft presents the $35,000 ceiling as a complete definition of a limited civil case rather than one of several conditions.
The filing destination, timing, and fee-waiver instructions lack supporting source texts.
“File” and “If you cannot afford the filing fee, ask” direct the reader to take procedural steps.

result.summary: The statutes support a general denial for an unverified complaint and the $35,000 ceiling. They do not establish PLD-050 eligibility, filing procedure, or fee-waiver instructions. Amount alone does not determine limited civil status.
